detail:

Arcus, the Robinhood Chain exchange developed by the team that built dYdX, has opened Multi-Asset Collateral to every trader with access to its perpetual futures, removing the trading-volume requirement that had limited the feature since October. The company announced the change on Thursday.

As in early access, Arcus caps deposits of assets other than USDG at $20,000 per user and $2 million across the platform. Each account can borrow at most $10,000, according to Arcus's public lending data, and the exchange rejects orders that would push a loan past that limit. By Unchained's math, 100 traders depositing the $20,000 maximum would fill the platform-wide cap.

Traders can now back perps positions with ether, held as wrapped ether (WETH), and nine stock tokens alongside USDG, which most Arcus traders had needed for perps margin until now. The stock tokens are SPY, QQQ, Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Meta and Tesla, the last seven of which the press release groups as "MAG7." Each asset carries a 50% initial loan-to-value ratio.

Get Unchained's crypto news in your inbox with the free Unchained Daily newsletter.

Early Access Began Oct. 19

Arcus started rolling out the feature on Oct. 19 to accounts with more than $25 million in trading volume on the exchange, with the same assets and the same 50% ratio. Other traders do not need to switch anything on, according to Thursday's post.

How the Loans Work

The borrowing is automatic: once tokens sit in the perps account, any margin or losses the trader's USDG doesn't cover become a variable-rate loan that shrinks as the margin need falls. That rate was 4.94% a year on Thursday, according to Arcus's public lending feed. If falling token prices or a growing loan push the account past a maintenance level set for each asset, or the loan exceeds the per-account cap, Arcus can liquidate it, closing perps positions, selling the tokens, or both.

"Spot positions and perpetuals positions shouldn't have to operate in separate silos," founder and CEO Eddie Zhang said in the press release. He said the feature lets traders put stock token value to work "whether they're looking to maintain an existing position, put on a new trade or hedge their exposure."

Arcus, in which Robinhood Crypto is a strategic investor, is not available in the U.S., Canada or the U.K. The exchange launched leveraged stock and crypto tokens in August, and Robinhood Wallet began routing stock token trades through it on Oct. 1.

title: Market Jitters? How Buffer ETFs Can Help Protect Your Portfolio
detail:
Market Jitters? How Buffer ETFs Can Help Protect Your Portfolio
Neena Mishra
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 10:04 AM PST 3 min read
QQQ
SPY
PJAN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Markets have been quite volatile lately, rattled by uncertainty over the potential payoffs from massive AI spending, midterm elections, and ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Against this backdrop, defined-outcome, or "buffer," ETFs, which offer upside participation up to a cap while cushioning downside losses, have seen surging investor demand.

This is one of the fastest-growing ETF categories, particularly since 2022, when both stocks and bonds delivered dismal returns.

How Buffer ETFs Work and What Investors Should Know

Buffer ETFs invest in a basket of FLEX options with varying strike prices. The strategy typically involves fund managers holding a customized combination of options. These include long call options to capture market upside, a put spread (buying one put option and selling another at a lower strike price) to provide downside protection, and a short call option at a higher strike price. Selling this call generates the premium needed to help pay for the downside protection. It also creates the upside cap.

Investors should focus on four key components when selecting a buffer ETF that fits their investment goals:

Reference Asset: The underlying index or ETF the fund tracks

Buffer Level: The amount of downside protection investors can choose upfront

Upside Cap: The maximum potential gain, determined at the beginning of the outcome period based on prevailing interest rates and market volatility

Outcome Period: The fixed period over which the cap and buffer apply

For example, the Innovator US Equity Power Buffer ETF PJAN aims to provide a 15% buffer against losses in US equities over a one-year period beginning each January, while allowing for upside participation up to a certain cap.

The caps and buffers apply from the first day to the last day of the outcome period. Investors who buy mid-period may experience different outcomes. At the end of the period, the ETF does not liquidate. Instead, it resets with a new cap and buffer for the following year.

The Trade-Off Between Downside Protection and Upside Potential

Investors should remember that stocks tend to rise over the long term and that short-term market noise is best ignored. Since its inception in January 1993, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF SPY has delivered an annualized return of 10.8%. The Nasdaq 100 ETF QQQ has generated an average annual return of 20.9% over the past 10 years. By seeking downside protection, however, investors give up any potential gains beyond the cap.

At the same time, many risk-averse investors, particularly those in or nearing retirement, have been reluctant to invest in stocks. As a result, significant amounts of cash remain parked in money market funds and other cash-like instruments.

title: Wall Street's Fear Gauge Just Made a Massive Move
detail:
Wall Street's Fear Gauge Just Made a Massive Move
Moz Farooque ACCA
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:22 AM PST 2 min read
^VIX
CL=F
^GSPC
^IXIC
^DJI

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Wall Street's fear gauge just posted its sharpest one-day drop in more than a year as investors moved quickly past the U.S. midterm elections.

The Cboe Volatility Index, or VIX, plunged 20.26% to 16.61 on Wednesday, its biggest one-day percentage decline since April 2025.

Is QQQ fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The move came as Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, removing one of the market's biggest near-term political unknowns.

U.S. stocks rallied alongside the collapse in volatility. The S&P 500 rose 1.6%, the Nasdaq gained 1.4%, and the Dow surged roughly 3%, as investors bet that divided government could reduce the likelihood of abrupt policy shifts from Washington.

Lower oil prices also helped.

Crude fell sharply as investors increasingly wagered that the election result could put pressure on President Donald Trump to de-escalate the Iran conflict. That helped push Treasury yields lower and gave equities another tailwind.

But the decline in the VIX does not mean every risk disappeared.

Democratic control could bring tougher scrutiny of AI data centers, energy companies, defense contractors and cryptocurrency, while debt-ceiling fights and government shutdown risks remain potential sources of volatility.

The sector reaction already showed that distinction.

Large hyperscalers including Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta gained, while data-center operators and semiconductor stocks came under pressure amid concerns that new infrastructure development could face tighter regulation.

Investor Takeaway

I think the VIX move matters because it shows investors were carrying a meaningful political uncertainty premium into the election.

Once the result became clear, that premium disappeared quickly.

A VIX at 16.61 is much closer to a normal risk environment than the elevated levels seen ahead of the vote, but it does not mean volatility is dead.

The market has simply moved from election uncertainty to policy uncertainty.

For investors, the key things to watch now are Treasury yields, oil prices, AI regulation, fiscal negotiations and whether the VIX can stay below 20 once the initial post-election relief trade fades.

The election removed one source of fear.

Wall Street now has to decide what replaces it.

Amazon (AMZN) shares were up more than 2% pre-bell and Uber (UBER) was 3% higher after the companies said they have partnered to offer Prime members free delivery on Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more through Amazon's website and app.

Healthcare

The State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) advanced 1%, the Vanguard Health Care Index Fund (VHT) was up 1.1%, while the iShares US Healthcare ETF (IYH) gained 1.5%. The iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB) was 0.8% higher.

Eli Lilly (LLY) stock was up more than 1% premarket after the company said it plans to present new clinical trial data on its investigational obesity drug retatrutide and research on combining Taltz and Zepbound.

Energy

The iShares US Energy ETF (IYE) fell 1.3%, while the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE) was up by 1.4%.

ConocoPhillips (COP) stock was up more than 1% before market open after the company reported higher Q3 adjusted earnings and revenue.

Commodities

Front-month US West Texas Intermediate crude oil gained 1.3% to reach $89.28 per barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange. Natural gas was down 1% at $2.93 per 1 million British Thermal Units. The United States Oil Fund (USO) increased by 1.4%, while the United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was 0.2% higher.

Gold futures for November rose 1.5% to $4,133.90 an ounce on the Comex. Silver futures advanced 0.9% to $52.75 an ounce. SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) was up 1.3%, and the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was 0.6% higher.

title: Stock Market Crash Or Rally? Plan For Both

Stock Market Crash Or Rally? Plan For Both

Part of our midterms guide. Start here: what the vote really changes for your money.

What Does Everyone Already Know?

On Monday, the Nasdaq 100 closed more than 10% below its Oct. 6 peak: a correction, its third this year. On Wednesday, after Democrats won Congress, the Dow rose 3.03% to 53,356, its best day since April 2025, and the S&P 500 rose 1.58% to 7,689.

Correction on Monday. Rally on Wednesday. Can you predict which one wins next week? Probably not. Nobody can, not reliably. But you can decide now what you'll do either way.

What Does The Data Say?

That this wasn't one market. It was two, moving in opposite directions at the same time. Look at Wednesday alone:

On the Dow's best day since April 2025, power stocks fell 9-14%. "The market" told you nothing about your stocks.

And the AI selloff kept going underneath the rally. In the month to Tuesday, AMD fell 24%, Micron 20%, Alphabet 18% and Dell 27%. On Wednesday, Micron fell another 7%. Meanwhile Centene, Wednesday's winner, was already up 96% over 12 months and just 5% below its 52-week high before the vote.

See more lines: why the two markets moved apart

The vote moved stocks on what a Democratic Congress might do in 2027: health-care money back (insurers and hospitals up), a smaller defense budget (defense down), scrutiny of AI data centers plus a Texas governor who wants to pause new ones (power and data-center builders down). None of those changed a single company's earnings on Wednesday; the new Congress isn't sworn in until January, and President Trump keeps his veto. The AI selloff is older and is about something else: whether roughly $900 billion of AI spending worldwide this year earns its money back. We'll score our own pre-vote calls in a day-after recap.

So Why Does This Feel So Hard?

Because fear and greed arrived on the same day. If you own Vistra, Wednesday felt like a crash. If you own Centene, it felt like a windfall. Both feelings push you to act on the price, right now.

We wrote about this frame in October, when inflation was the fear: Inflation Is Back. Is A Stock Market Crash Next? The point then holds now. Crashes happen: in 2022, the S&P 500 fell 25% from its January high, Nvidia fell 63% and Meta fell 74%. And recoveries happen faster than people expect: after the 1982 low, the S&P 500 rose 58% in a year. Often, the investors who got hurt most weren't the ones who owned the wrong stocks. They were the ones who had to decide what to do in the middle of the move.
